metadata.note: Fresno's second mainline and the modern service that replaced it. The San Francisco & San Joaquin Valley Railroad (the 'People's Railroad') was built 1895-98 with public subscription to break Southern Pacific's grip on the valley; it reached Fresno October 5, 1896 and Bakersfield May 27, 1898, and Santa Fe bought it before the end of 1898, making it the Valley Division. The Southern Pacific's own valley trunk through Fresno is covered separately by cprr_sacramento_fresno.geojson and sp_tehachapi_fresno_la.geojson, so between them Fresno now shows both of the competing mainlines it actually had. Note the 1971-1974 gap: Amtrak's initial network sent Los Angeles-San Francisco trains over the Coast Line, so the whole valley lost passenger rail until the San Joaquin began on March 6, 1974 - renamed Gold Runner in 2025. CONVENTION: a line's first opening is shown in its opening year, while later extensions and frequency changes take effect in the year they held for the majority of; exact dates are in every segment note. NOT DRAWN: Santa Fe later extended west from Stockton to a deepwater terminal at Point Richmond on San Francisco Bay, but that date is not sourced here, so the historic stages stop at Stockton; the modern Gold Runner features do show the Richmond-Oakland end. Geometry is real OSM track; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates, not from GTFS.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_and_San_Joaquin_Valley_Railroad (the 'People's Railroad' backed by Claus Spreckels, built up the San Joaquin Valley and absorbed by the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Joaquins (Amtrak restored San Joaquin Valley service in 1974 and it grew by stages to the present multiple daily round trips, with Sacramento service added later)

segments.note: Amtrak restored San Joaquin Valley service on March 6, 1974 (inaugural run March 5) with one daily round trip, Bakersfield-Oakland. Amtrak picked the Santa Fe route over the Southern Pacific for its higher speed (79 vs 70 mph) and lighter freight congestion. The train cannot run south of Bakersfield because of capacity limits over the Tehachapi Loop.
